steps.message: The build succeeds. Here is the final patch:

## Diagnosis

The defect was in the password-setup logic, where checking **"Show password"** disabled the confirmation field *and* made it an accepted substitute for actually confirming the password.

`CustomAuthenticatedSlide.java` (first-time setup intro slide):
- The checkbox listener called `_textPasswordConfirm.setEnabled(false)` — the confirm field became un-fillable.
- `isPolicyRespected()` returned `areEditTextsEqual(...) || _checkPasswordVisibility.isChecked()` — so with the box checked, any non-empty password satisfied the slide policy and AppIntro let the user proceed straight to the main screen with no confirmation.
- `onUserIllegallyRequestedNextPage()` had the same `&& !isChecked()` escape hatch.

The identical pattern existed in `Dialogs.showSetPasswordDialog()` (used when adding a password slot later), where the OK button was enabled via `equal || switchToggleVisibility.isChecked()`.

## Fix

1. **`EditTextHelper`** — added `setEditTextPasswordVisibility(boolean, EditText...)`, which toggles `PasswordTransformationMethod` on *all* supplied fields (preserving the cursor/selection) and never disables them.
2. **`CustomAuthenticatedSlide`** — the checkbox now reveals both the password and confirmation fields instead of disabling the confirmation field; `isPolicyRespected()` is now simply `areEditTextsEqual(_textPassword, _textPasswordConfirm)` (which already enforces non-empty), and the error-message branch no longer exempts the checked state, so the "passwords do not match" snackbar shows correctly.
3. **`Dialogs.showSetPasswordDialog`** — same treatment: shared visibility helper, and both the OK-button enablement and the click handler now require a matching confirmation unconditionally. Removed the now-unused `PasswordTransformationMethod` imports.

Confirmation is now mandatory in every path, regardless of the "show password" state, while revealing the password still works as intended (and now reveals both fields, which is more useful than greying one out).

Verified with `./gradlew clean assembleDebug` → **BUILD SUCCESSFUL**.

## Diagnosis

The defect was in the password-setup logic, where checking **"Show password"** disabled the confirmation field *and* made it an accepted substitute for actually confirming the password.

`CustomAuthenticatedSlide.java` (first-time setup intro slide):
- The checkbox listener called `_textPasswordConfirm.setEnabled(false)` — the confirm field became un-fillable.
- `isPolicyRespected()` returned `areEditTextsEqual(...) || _checkPasswordVisibility.isChecked()` — so with the box checked, any non-empty password satisfied the slide policy and AppIntro let the user proceed straight to the main screen with no confirmation.
- `onUserIllegallyRequestedNextPage()` had the same `&& !isChecked()` escape hatch.

The identical pattern existed in `Dialogs.showSetPasswordDialog()` (used when adding a password slot later), where the OK button was enabled via `equal || switchToggleVisibility.isChecked()`.

## Fix

1. **`EditTextHelper`** — added `setEditTextPasswordVisibility(boolean, EditText...)`, which toggles `PasswordTransformationMethod` on *all* supplied fields (preserving the cursor/selection) and never disables them.
2. **`CustomAuthenticatedSlide`** — the checkbox now reveals both the password and confirmation fields instead of disabling the confirmation field; `isPolicyRespected()` is now simply `areEditTextsEqual(_textPassword, _textPasswordConfirm)` (which already enforces non-empty), and the error-message branch no longer exempts the checked state, so the "passwords do not match" snackbar shows correctly.
3. **`Dialogs.showSetPasswordDialog`** — same treatment: shared visibility helper, and both the OK-button enablement and the click handler now require a matching confirmation unconditionally. Removed the now-unused `PasswordTransformationMethod` imports.

Confirmation is now mandatory in every path, regardless of the "show password" state, while revealing the password still works as intended (and now reveals both fields, which is more useful than greying one out).

Verified with `./gradlew clean assembleDebug` → **BUILD SUCCESSFUL**.
